# Preface {.unnumbered}

This handbook is for people who teach economics and want to use a coding agent to prepare and run a module. It covers lecture material, problem sets and code labs, assessment design, marking, checking and the rules that apply at UK universities, together with version control, reusable skills and automation.

No programming is needed to follow it. Chapter 1 marks the level each chapter assumes, and chapters 2 to 11 are enough to start.

The main text does not depend on a particular product. Notes headed *In Claude Code* give the specifics for that tool. Those notes, and the university policies cited, were checked on 26 and 27 November 2026 and will date.

The [templates](chapters/templates.qmd) at the end of the handbook are also files in the `templates/` folder of the repository. None has been tested on a live module.

Comments and corrections are welcome as issues on the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/WhitesPhD/coding-agents-teaching-handbook), in particular examples from theory, macroeconomics and applied modules.

The handbook gives general guidance, not legal advice. Your own institution's policy takes precedence.
